stem.en: In a bipolar junction transistor, the most heavily doped region is the:

explanation.en: The emitter must inject a large number of charge carriers into the base, so it is the most heavily doped region.

stem.en: The base of a transistor is made thin and lightly doped so that:

options.en: most carriers injected by the emitter cross over to the collector
the base can dissipate more heat
the transistor works without any bias

explanation.en: A thin, lightly doped base gives few chances for recombination, so about 95–99% of the injected carriers reach the collector.

stem.en: In the circuit symbol of an NPN transistor, the arrow on the emitter points:

explanation.en: The arrow shows the direction of conventional emitter current. In NPN it points out of the base ("Not Pointing iN").

stem.en: Physically, the largest of the three regions of a transistor is the:

explanation.en: The collector is made largest because most of the power (heat) is dissipated at the collector–base junction.

stem.en: A bipolar junction transistor has:

explanation.en: A BJT is a three-layer device (NPN or PNP), so it has two junctions: emitter–base and collector–base.

explanation.en: In the active region the emitter–base junction is forward biased and the collector–base junction is reverse biased.

Which transistor configuration gives a 180° phase shift between input and output voltages?

explanation.en: In the CE amplifier the output voltage is inverted with respect to the input, a phase shift of 180°.

stem.en: The common collector configuration is also called:

explanation.en: In CC the output is taken from the emitter and follows the input voltage (voltage gain ≈ 1), hence "emitter follower".

stem.en: The configuration with the highest input impedance is:

explanation.en: Common collector has a very high input impedance and a low output impedance, which is why it is used as a buffer.

The input characteristic of a transistor in CE configuration is a graph of:

options.en: I_B against V_BE at constant V_CE
I_C against V_CE at constant I_B
I_C against I_B at constant V_CE
I_E against V_CB at constant I_C

explanation.en: Input characteristics plot base current against base–emitter voltage, with V_CE kept constant.

stem.en: A transistor is in the saturation region when:

options.en: E–B is forward and C–B is reverse biased
E–B is reverse and C–B is forward biased

explanation.en: In saturation both junctions are forward biased, V_CE is very small (about 0.2 V) and I_C is at its maximum.

stem.en: In the cut-off region of a transistor:

options.en: I_B ≈ 0 and only a small leakage current flows in the collector

explanation.en: In cut-off both junctions are reverse biased, I_B ≈ 0 and only the leakage current I_CEO flows, so V_CE ≈ V_CC.

stem.en: When the base current of a CE transistor changes by 10 µA, the collector current changes by 1.2 mA at constant V_CE. The ac current gain β is:

explanation.en: β_ac = ΔI_C/ΔI_B = 1.2 mA/10 µA = 1200 µA/10 µA = 120.

stem.en: In the active region, the output characteristic curves of a CE transistor rise slightly with V_CE. This is mainly due to:

explanation.en: As V_CE rises, the C–B depletion layer widens and the effective base width decreases, so fewer carriers recombine and I_C rises slightly. This is the Early effect.

stem.en: When a transistor is used as a switch, it is operated in the:

explanation.en: As a switch the transistor is either fully OFF (cut-off) or fully ON (saturation).

stem.en: For use as a linear amplifier, the transistor must operate in the:

explanation.en: Only in the active region is I_C proportional to I_B, so the output is a faithful, amplified copy of the input.

stem.en: In a CE amplifier β = 50, the load resistance is 4 kΩ and the input resistance is 1 kΩ. The magnitude of the voltage gain is:

explanation.en: A_v = β R_L / r_i = 50 × 4 kΩ / 1 kΩ = 200 (with a 180° phase shift).

stem.en: In an NPN transistor switch (CE), the input at the base is made HIGH. The collector output is:

explanation.en: A HIGH input saturates the transistor, so V_CE ≈ V_CE(sat) ≈ 0.2 V: the output is LOW. The circuit acts as a NOT gate.

stem.en: A transistor has β = 99 in the CE configuration. Its current gain γ in the CC configuration is:
Which transistor configuration has a voltage gain of about 1, the highest input impedance and the lowest output impedance?

explanation.en: The common collector (emitter follower) has voltage gain ≈ 1, very high input impedance and very low output impedance, so it is used as a buffer.

stem.en: A transistor switch has V_CC = 12 V, R_C = 2 kΩ and β = 150. Taking V_CE(sat) ≈ 0, the minimum base current needed to saturate it is:

explanation.en: I_C(sat) ≈ V_CC/R_C = 12 V/2 kΩ = 6 mA. I_B(min) = I_C(sat)/β = 6 mA/150 = 0.04 mA = 40 µA.
